title: Public sympathy over shootings is misplaced
article: A letter from Shawn LeBleu, Lethbridge.

Here we go again. A police officer is required to use force to bring down a criminal. What is the public response? Sympathy, as usual. The problem is much of the sympathy is not directed toward the officer who had to go through this ordeal; it is for the guy who stabbed two other people, and came at a police officer with the same bloody knife, after being asked numerous times to drop his weapon.

Why is it so difficult to understand? If you threaten a police officer with a weapon, he will shoot you, and not in the leg. Real life is not the Wild West, nor it like an Eddie Murphy movie where you will get shot in the pinkie toe. They will shoot you in the middle of the chest as many times as it takes for you to drop. That is what they are trained to do. That is what they should do.
I feel sympathy for the officer who has to deal with this tragedy for the rest of his life.
I feel for the family of the guy who thought it was OK to pull a weapon on a cop.
I feel sympathy for all Calgary police officers who have to go out every day and protect people by putting their lives on the line. I don't feel sorry for the criminal.
